h1: Storm & Hail Damage Roof Repair in Mission, TX
lede: Edel Roofing & Construction inspects and repairs Mission roofs hurt by hail, high wind and heavy rain. The inspection is free, and you get photos and a written report to give your insurer.

sections.title: Storms that have hit Mission
paras: Mission has taken several damaging storms in the last ten years. National Weather Service reports include:

May 31, 2016: a downburst near Palmview and Mission with winds estimated at 85 to 95 mph that damaged more than 150 homes and businesses. July 25, 2020: Hurricane Hanna dropped 14.40 inches of rain on Mission, with 60 to 65 mph gusts along Interstate 2, and damaged hundreds of poorly built homes and other buildings, mostly their roofs. April 21, 2023: spotters reported hail up to 2.5 inches in Mission and 2.75 inches in Peñitas. April 29, 2023: wind flipped food trucks near Bryan Rd and Business 83. May 29, 2023: hail near 0.88 inches about a mile east of town.
Hail sizes come from spotters, so they are estimates. Hail over 1 inch is big enough to crack shingles, and Mission has had it more than once.

sections.title: Storm damage we inspect for in Mission

cards.title: Hail impacts
cards.body: Cracked and bruised shingles, missing granules, and dents in vents, gutters, and flashing.

cards.title: Wind damage
cards.body: Missing shingles, broken seals, and lifted ridge caps. On flat roofs, membrane pulled back at the edges.

cards.title: Rain intrusion
cards.body: Water that got in during a long, heavy rain, found through stains, damp insulation, or soft decking.

cards.title: Older roof wear
cards.body: Many Mission homes have their original 2000s roof. A storm that only scuffs a new roof can finish an old one.

sections.title: After a storm in Mission: what to do
paras: First, look for active leaks and protect what is inside. Then take photos of any damage you can see from the ground, including gutters, screens, and cars, with the date. Call your insurance company to report it and ask about the deadline for your policy.

Get the roof inspected before you agree to any work. The Texas Department of Insurance suggests getting more than one bid, checking references, and not paying in full up front. In Texas it is illegal for a contractor to waive or rebate your deductible.

Hidalgo County is outside the TWIA coastal area, so your claim goes through your regular homeowners policy, not the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association. We document what we find with photos and a written report. We are not a public adjuster; the claim decision is between you and your insurer.

sections.title: How a Mission storm inspection works

cards.title: 1. Call
cards.body: Call (956) 422-3335 or book online. We come from Edinburg, about 26 minutes away.

cards.title: 2. Inspect
cards.body: We walk every slope and check the attic if there are signs of water inside.

cards.title: 3. Report
cards.body: You get photos and a written report, and we tell you if the damage is cosmetic.

cards.title: 4. Estimate
cards.body: If repair or replacement is needed, you get a written estimate before any work.

sections.title: Why Mission homeowners call Edel after a storm

faqs.q: A storm came through but I don't see damage. Do I need an inspection?
faqs.a: If there was hail over about an inch or strong wind on your street, yes. Hail bruises and broken seals do not show from the ground. The inspection is free.

faqs.q: Will my insurance pay for a new roof?
faqs.a: If a covered storm damaged a large part of the roof, the claim may pay for much of a replacement, minus your deductible. If the damage is small, it may be a repair. We document it; your insurer decides.

faqs.q: My roof is old. Will the insurer blame age instead of the storm?
faqs.a: Insurers look at both. Age wear is even across the roof; hail and wind leave a pattern. Photos and a written report help show what the storm did.

faqs.q: Do you fix the damage or just inspect?
faqs.a: Both. We repair storm damage and replace roofs when needed. See roof repair and roof replacement in Mission.

faqs.q: How do I book a storm inspection in Mission?
faqs.a: Call (956) 422-3335 or book an inspection online. It is free, with no obligation.
